subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Write the reactions of F₂ and Cl₂ with water.

verification.note: Unit 9 (VIIA Group Elements) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.86-89, the sub-box "VIIA GROUP ELEMENTS" of printed chapter 7, which prints the question and a model answer. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK ARROW CORRECTED (book p.86, VSAQ 3): the printed answer writes the chlorine reaction as Cl₂ + H₂O → HCl + HClO with a single arrow. That reaction is reversible and is written here with ⇌. All four printed equations were atom-counted and balance as printed. NOTATION: the book writes the same acid as HClO in the equation and the oxoacid section prints it as HOCl; HOCl is used throughout this unit. PRINTED WORDING: the question is printed "Write the reactions F₂ and Cl₂ with water?"; the word "of" is added and the question mark replaced by a full stop, because the printed line is not a question.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Fluorine with water
lines: Fluorine oxidises water and sets oxygen free.
With a small amount of water, ozone is
steps.why: Fluorine is the strongest oxidising agent of the halogens, so it takes electrons from the oxygen of water and sets that oxygen free. Both equations balance: the first has 4 F, 4 H and 2 O on each side, the second 6 F, 6 H and 3 O.
common_mistakes: Writing the product as HF₂ or F₂H. The product is hydrogen fluoride, HF.
Writing F₂ + H₂O → HF + O₂ without coefficients. That line does not balance; 2F₂ + 2H₂O is needed for 4HF and one O₂.
steps.memory_tip: Fluorine takes the oxygen out of water: plenty of water gives O₂, little water gives O₃.
steps.margin_note: One balanced fluorine equation earns this mark. The ozone equation is the extra line that shows the reaction is understood.

steps.label: Chlorine with water
lines: Chlorine reacts with water only partly, and
In sunlight the HOCl decomposes and gives
steps.why: Chlorine is a weaker oxidising agent than fluorine, so it does not set oxygen free from water at once. It disproportionates: one chlorine atom goes to −1 in HCl and the other to +1 in HOCl. Only when the HOCl decomposes in sunlight is oxygen released. The two sunlight equations are printed as the overall change from Cl₂ and water, not as the decomposition of HOCl on its own: adding HOCl → HCl + [O] to the reversible line gives Cl₂ + H₂O → 2HCl + [O], and doubling that, with the two oxygen atoms joining as O₂, gives 2Cl₂ + 2H₂O → 4HCl + O₂. The oxidising order F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂ has no exception, and it is why the two halogens behave differently here.
common_mistakes: Writing Cl₂ + H₂O → HCl + HOCl with a single arrow. That reaction is reversible, so the sign is ⇌; the sunlight decomposition after it is not reversible.
Writing that chlorine releases O₂ from water directly, as fluorine does. Chlorine gives HCl and HOCl first.
steps.memory_tip: Fluorine takes the oxygen; chlorine only splits into HCl and HOCl.
steps.margin_note: The reversible equation is the marked line. Add the sunlight line only if there is room.

insider_note: Most marks are lost by giving chlorine the fluorine answer. Fluorine releases oxygen from water; chlorine disproportionates into HCl and HOCl.
